_comment: Scene-mechanism palette, dealt ONE-per-chapter by src/librarian/sceneMechanismPlan.ts. This is the FUNCTIONAL MOVE the chapter's marquee scene dramatizes — the dramatic transaction (WHO acts and what changes between people/forces). It is an axis ORTHOGONAL to scene SHAPE (config/scene-shapes.json = the narrative grammar: postmortem/dialogue/contrast/…) and to STANCE (sceneModePlan = the temporal vantage: live/retrospective/…): one move can be rendered as dialogue OR postmortem, live OR retrospective. PREVENTION-only: cross-chapter DEVICE reuse (e.g. 'a leader loses her voice, a substitute seizes the teaching prop and teaches' recurring across ch3/8/11; a message 'restarted/reframed' reused as the example move) is a scene_skeleton/repeated_unit class with NO deterministic adherence gate — the model QC sweep is the backstop. The author fills each move with THIS chapter's own concept and people; it constrains the transaction, not the wording. Keep >= 9 entries AND a palette size coprime with sceneMechanismPlan's CHAPTER_STEP (currently 10 entries, step 3) so round-robin spreads each move and holds any one well under the share cap.

mechanisms.directive: FUNCTIONAL MOVE = THE PROTAGONIST DECIDES ALONE. One person carries the call with no one to defer to; the scene is them owning a choice and living its consequence. NOT a mentor handing them the answer.

FUNCTIONAL MOVE = TWO EQUALS DISAGREE, ONE YIELDS. Two people of equal standing hold opposing reads; the turn is one genuinely conceding — not being overruled by a senior, not a mentor correcting a junior.

FUNCTIONAL MOVE = THE EXPERT HITS THEIR OWN LIMIT. The most competent person in the scene reaches the edge of what they know or can do and says so; the lesson is in the admission. NOT someone else catching their error.

FUNCTIONAL MOVE = THE OUTSIDER SEES IT. Someone new, peripheral, or junior notices what the practiced insiders have stopped seeing. The fresh-eyes observation is the hinge. NOT an expert teaching the newcomer.
FUNCTIONAL MOVE = ONE SMALL ACT CASCADES. A minor, almost-overlooked action sets off a disproportionate chain; the scene tracks the cascade from its tiny cause. NOT a big dramatic decision.
FUNCTIONAL MOVE = THE RULE MEETS ITS EXCEPTION. A reliable rule, habit, or process is applied and the one case it does not fit appears; the scene IS the collision, not the patch afterward.

FUNCTIONAL MOVE = OFFERED HELP IS REFUSED, THEN RESHAPED. One person offers help, advice, or a tool; it is declined or it flatly fails; the turn is the offer being reshaped into something that finally lands. NOT a clean teaching handoff.

FUNCTIONAL MOVE = A STATED COMMITMENT IS TESTED. Someone has declared an intention, value, or plan; the scene puts its real cost in front of them in the moment and shows whether it holds. NOT a calm retrospective review.

FUNCTIONAL MOVE = THE COST IS PAID FIRST. Someone pays a real, visible cost (gives something up, takes the hit, does the unglamorous part) BEFORE any payoff arrives; the scene sits in that gap. NOT a reward that lands immediately.

FUNCTIONAL MOVE = A TOOL OR METHOD IS MISAPPLIED. A real method, framework, or instrument is used wrongly first; the correction is the lesson. The center of gravity is the misuse, not the person who fixes it.
